envelope.text: `std::shared_ptr<ServerGoalHandle>`; this callback receives the 16-byte goal id

why:
installs the hook that fires once an accepted goal's accept reply has reached the client -- rclcpp_action's `handle_accepted`, which is where a deferred goal is supposed to start executing. Added by issue 0796: until then a C++ user who returned `ACCEPT_AND_DEFER` was never told the goal had been accepted, so the capability C and Rust had was missing here. Fires for `ACCEPT_AND_EXECUTE` and `ACCEPT_AND_DEFER` alike. Setter, and stateless, for the reasons `cpp:Server::set_goal_callback` gives; upstream hands the callback an owning `ServerGoalHandle` where ours passes the goal id, because our goals live in a static arena (see `cpp:Server::for_each_active_goal`).

phase-428 (RFC-0089): re-keyed by the namespace flip. `nros::ActionClient<A>` / `nros::ActionServer<A>` are now aliases of `rclcpp_action::Client<A>` / `rclcpp_action::Server<A>`, which the extractor keys as `Client::*` / `Server::*`. The type is `same` now and the member is `ours-only`, so it no longer inherits its type's verdict and carries its own.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the setter's doc comment states the goal-id argument against upstream's owning `ServerGoalHandle`; statelessness was already stated on the class and on `set_goal_callback`.
